transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-03-15
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~60 minutes
Attendees: Liam Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Carlos Mendoza (Equinox CTO), Ruth Kim (Infra Lead), Daniel Park (Security), Maya Singh (PM)

[00:00] Liam: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro, I'm Liam on the account team, and Priya is our solutions engineer. how's everyone doing?
[00:06] Carlos: Doing well, thanks. we wanted to walk through our network/security constraints for a Private deployment. HIPAA environment, so data residency and key management are top of mind.
[00:12] Priya: Yeah totally. can you kick us off with your high-level goals and which workloads you want in the private VPC?
[00:20] Maya: Sure. We want inference for clinical note summarization and an embeddings index for search. Latency target p50 ~150-200ms, p95 under 600ms for short prompts. We also need everything to stay in our AWS accounts or in a managed private deployment in our VPC.
[00:36] Ruth: To add, we require either VPC peering or PrivateLink — we don't want any public internet egress for requests or payloads. Also region constraint: primary in us-east-1, secondary in eu-west-1 for European patient data.
[00:50] Priya: Cool that's helpful. Redwood Private supports both VPC peering and PrivateLink (AWS interface endpoints). There are tradeoffs: peering is simpler for intra-account communication but can hit routing/overlap limitations; PrivateLink keeps control on your side and is cross-account friendly.
[01:05] Daniel: How do you handle KMS? we have an HSM-backed key in our account and want to manage keys locally for audit reasons.
[01:12] Priya: We support customer-managed KMS keys for data-at-rest encryption. For Private, the control plane can be customer-managed as well — we can integrate with your KMS via cross-account grants, or you can bring keys into the private deployment. We'll document the exact permissions.
[01:26] Carlos: Is there any telemetry that leaves our VPC? e.g., logs or metrics that Redwood collects?
[01:31] Liam: Good question. In Private mode, logs and metrics can be routed to your CloudWatch/CloudTrail/S3 buckets; Redwood will not retain customer payloads by default. We can also disable sending model telemetry off-net if required for compliance.
[01:44] Ruth: About network flow, do requests go out to a public endpoint then back in, or can we keep an internal endpoint?
[01:50] Priya: You can have an interface endpoint (PrivateLink) that gives you a private DNS name inside your VPC. Alternatively, with VPC peering you’d route directly to our service VPC. For strict no-internet policies we recommend PrivateLink or an inter-account peering + Transit Gateway.
[02:06] Maya: Any constraints on regions? We have some regulatory requirements that patient data in EU must not leave eu-west-1.
[02:13] Priya: Redwood can deploy Private control planes and inference nodes in specific regions. For eu data we can run the private deployment in eu-west-1 — we just need the appropriate capacity and GPU availability there. A note: some newer GPU types or quantized kernels may have different latency/cost profiles per region.
[02:30] Daniel: For the PoC, we want to keep it simple. what's the minimal setup to run a benchmark in our VPC?
[02:36] Priya: Minimal: a VPC with two private subnets, a security group allowing inbound from your app subnets to the interface endpoint, an IAM role for the SE to access your test buckets, and optionally a KMS key grant. We'll provide a CloudFormation/Terraform snippet.
[02:50] Carlos: Do we need NAT gateways? Will the nodes require outbound internet access for container images or model downloads?
[02:57] Priya: For Private deployments we support two modes: pre-baked image deployment where we ship model artifacts into your VPC so no outbound is required, or a pull model where the nodes pull images from an internal registry. If you want fully air-gapped, we can coordinate image transfer; otherwise you may need a controlled egress path.
[03:14] Ruth: Sounds good. on the security side: SSO/SAML and RBAC — can we hook into our Okta directory for user access to the control plane?
[03:21] Liam: Yes, Redwood Private supports SSO (SAML) and SCIM for user provisioning. RBAC roles map to your groups. Audit logs are available and can be forwarded to your SIEM.
[03:31] Daniel: Are audit logs tamper-evident? We need to show chain-of-custody for production requests.
[03:36] Priya: We can forward logs to your S3 with object-lock policies and CloudTrail. For higher assurance, you can use customer-managed KMS keys and CloudWatch log stream protections; we'll include recommended configurations in the security doc.
[03:50] Maya: On the performance side, what's the expected latency differential between Hosted and Private?
[03:55] Priya: If you colocate in the same region and use PrivateLink, latency is comparable to Hosted because the network hop is small. Dedicated GPU pools with pinned models usually give better p95 characteristics vs noisy multi-tenant hosted. We typically see p50s in the 100-200ms ballpark for short prompts on optimized models; p95 depends a lot on batch size and KV cache warmness.
[04:15] Carlos: We care about deterministic performance for SLAs. Do you offer reserved capacity or dedicated pools?
[04:20] Liam: Yes — Redwood Dedicated offers reserved GPU pools with autoscaling policies and SLA-backed latency/availability. For Private deployments you can reserve capacity inside your deployment or connect to Redwood Dedicated nodes in a hybrid model.
[04:33] Ruth: Cost question: is Private more expensive than Hosted per token?
[04:36] Liam: Typically Private incurs additional infra costs — more for dedicated GPUs, egress, and management — but we provide unit economics and batching/quantization recommendations to reduce per-token cost. We'll share a pricing matrix.
[04:49] Daniel: If we do VPC peering across accounts we sometimes run into CIDR overlap issues. Does Redwood require specific CIDR ranges?
[04:55] Priya: We recommend non-overlapping RFC1918 /16 or /20 ranges; if overlap happens we can use PrivateLink to avoid routing conflicts. We'll include an example peering plan in the diagram.
[05:06] Carlos: Any known limits or compliance gotchas with eu-west-1 region?
[05:11] Priya: Mostly it's capacity — some GPU types are limited. Also networking features like AWS Global Accelerator are region-limited. For HIPAA compliance in EU we'd pair eu-west-1 deployments with stricter data handling. We'll surface any regional limitations in the runbook.
[05:25] Maya: Ok timeline: we want a PoC in 1 week if possible, but realistically 2-3 weeks. Thoughts?
[05:31] Priya: For a lightweight benchmark, 1 week is doable if you can provision a VPC and grant the SE limited access to test S3 buckets and a KMS key grant. For a full private deployment we estimate 4–8 weeks including security review and infra changes.
[05:44] Ruth: What's involved on our side for the PoC — minimal list?
[05:48] Priya: We'll need: test VPC/subnets, IAM role for SE, test dataset in S3, KMS test key or temporary permissions, and an app-side test harness that hits the private endpoint. We'll send Terraform/CloudFormation snippets.
[05:59] Daniel: Regarding fallback: if dedicated nodes go down or capacity is constrained, can traffic route to Hosted temporarily?
[06:05] Liam: Yes — we support smart routing and automatic fallback to compatible model variants in Hosted or lower-capacity tiers. That can be configured per-route with failover policies. For strict isolation customers sometimes opt out of fallback.
[06:18] Carlos: We want to see the SOC 2 and architecture docs before engaging security formally.
[06:22] Liam: We'll attach SOC 2 type II, penetration test summaries, and the Private architecture runbook.
[06:27] Maya: Anything else from the team?
[06:30] Ruth: One more — outbound IP allowlist. If our firewall needs fixed egress IPs, can Redwood provide them?
[06:35] Priya: For PrivateLink you will initiate the endpoint; egress is under your control. For peering we can provide the set of service IP ranges used by the deployment; for Dedicated we can help reserve Elastic IPs or use NAT with static egress. We'll detail options.
[06:50] Liam: Ok, let's recap next steps quickly. Priya will send the architecture diagram with peering/PrivateLink/Transit Gateway patterns, plus CloudFormation snippets. I'll follow up with pricing and reserved capacity options. Daniel/Ruth will share the KMS/endpoint requirements and provision the test VPC so we can aim for a PoC week of 2027-03-22.
[07:10] Carlos: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[07:13] Maya: Thanks.
[07:15] Liam: Appreciate your time. We'll send follow-up by EOD tomorrow with the docs attachments.

Notes about transcript quality: a few transcription artifacts — 'KV cash' appears once (should be KV cache), and Speaker labels sometimes merged (Speaker 1/Speaker 2) but context preserved. Links referenced: Redwood Private runbook (link provided in follow-up), SOC2 report (will be shared as PDF).
